index_title: Finite-fibre kernels, hidden projections and named-axis Goursat codes
scope: Preparation for OTHER Lean projects. The three kernel/CSP/relative-homogeneity/duality results remaining in finite_packet_kernel_constraints.tex and the two selected entire-named-axis results give five exports and eight auxiliary equations. The affine translate lemma from the kernel file is already prepared in rigid_groupoid and is not re-exported. Other simultaneous-quotient results remain outside scope.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Intrinsic groups, actual binding marginals and finite projections are different objects; no CCO, SAP, symmetry, exactness, owner homogeneity or finite projection is assumed implicitly.

assumptions.name: Relational arity at most two
assumptions.statement: An actual structure X in a relational language, possibly infinite, whose relations have arity at most two. Unary predicates, binary loops and both ordered cross directions are included; nullary relations impose no permutation constraint. No functions or named constants are added. No homogeneity, CCO, symmetry, SAP or exactness is assumed.

assumptions.name: Invariant finite-fibre partition of the whole universe
assumptions.statement: F is an Aut(X)-invariant equivalence partition of ALL points into finite classes C. The classes are nonempty as quotient classes, but the class family may be empty if X is empty. Individual classes may be unnamed and may move under automorphisms.

assumptions.name: Countability for finite exhaustion and separation
assumptions.statement: X is countable. Its family of nonempty finite classes and the direct sum of their finite duals are countable. Used for the explicit finite-solution tree and the explicit countable linear-functional extension. Global binary patching and homogeneity-based finite extensions do not need it.

assumptions.name: Optional relative owner homogeneity
assumptions.statement: The expansion X^own naming EVERY F-class by its own unary predicate is homogeneous. This is an extra hypothesis, not a consequence of original homogeneity or merely adding the predicates.

assumptions.name: Elementary abelian INTRINSIC groups
assumptions.statement: Each full intrinsic H_C=Aut(X restricted to C) is identified with a finite F2-vector space V_C. Do not replace V_C by the actual binding image B_C without proof. The local H_CD need not be subdirect.

assumptions.name: Entire finite named sorts in a homogeneous source
assumptions.statement: For the separate entire-axis results, X is homogeneous and has pairwise disjoint entire finite named sorts P_i. They need not exhaust the universe; other named sorts may be infinite. The acting group is FULL Aut(X), not the possibly smaller image of an earlier finer source.

assumptions.name: Elementary abelian named-sort intrinsic groups
assumptions.statement: Only for the Goursat/rank branch, each R_i=Aut(X restricted to the entire named P_i) is a finite F2-vector space V_i. Flat transport for graph pair groups only needs the general full-group image and graph-isomorphism hypotheses.

assumptions.name: Elementary finite algebra and classical choices
assumptions.statement: Finite permutations, groups, subspaces, finite-dimensional annihilators and rank-nullity. The finite tree path and countable functional-extension arguments are proved in the notes; no external compactness, Konig or algebraic separation theorem is left unexpanded.

definitions.name: Actual relational source and full group
definitions.statement: Gamma=Aut(X) consists of actual bijections preserving every relation in both directions.

definitions.name: Owner class action and kernel
definitions.statement: Gamma permutes F-classes by invariance. N is the kernel of that action: it fixes every class setwise, not every real point.

definitions.name: Intrinsic local motion groups
definitions.statement: H_C is the full automorphism group of the finite induced fibre. H_CD consists of pairs whose union is an induced automorphism of C union D fixing each fibre setwise. These are not presumed actual global projections.

definitions.name: Finite local solutions
definitions.statement: Sol(S) consists of H_C-tuples on finite S satisfying every H_CD condition for different fibres; the union acts on the finite full fibre union.

definitions.name: Restriction representation and actual marginals
definitions.statement: rho:N->product H_C restricts each actual owner-kernel automorphism to all fibres. B_C=pr_C rho(N), P_CD=pr_CD rho(N). Set equalities with product families mean equality under this specified group isomorphism.

definitions.name: Owner-named expansion
definitions.statement: X^own adds a separate unary predicate for EVERY F-class. Its automorphism group is exactly N; homogeneity is a separate A04 premise.

definitions.name: Finite-support test space and local row span
definitions.statement: D is direct sum V_C*, embedded as finitely supported linear tests on the full product. R is the span of annihilator rows defining the actual H_CD; unary-supported rows must be valid local equations, not freely added restrictions.

definitions.name: Restricted support tests and annihilators
definitions.statement: D_S is the finite direct sum on S, included into D by zero extension. Ann(pr_S N) is viewed in D_S and compared to R intersect D_S in that precise embedding.

definitions.name: Entire named-sort restrictions
definitions.statement: For A06, R_i is the intrinsic automorphism group on P_i and P_ij the ACTUAL pair image of full Gamma. No finite-fibre F partition is needed in this branch.

definitions.name: Finite Goursat check map
definitions.statement: For finite S and elementary abelian R_i, choose common quotient spaces W_ij for each actual subdirect pair group. Phi_S has pair components pi_ij(x_i)+rho_ij(x_j), with one chosen orientation for each finite pair.

definitions.name: Hidden parity and moving-owner controls
definitions.statement: Use the actual binary orbital structures of the four-fibre parity-shift group and of left-regular S3. The former is nonhomogeneous; the latter is homogeneous but its individually owner-named expansion is not. Neither is declared an exact CCO source.

claims.name: Invariant owner action and normal kernel
claims.statement: Every original automorphism induces a permutation of the invariant F-classes; this is a group action and its kernel N is a normal subgroup. Classes may move in Gamma, while N fixes them individually setwise.

claims.name: Local intrinsic and pair groups
claims.statement: H_C and H_CD are finite permutation groups, with H_CD a subgroup of H_C times H_D. Preservation includes unary instances, within-fibre loops and both directions of cross relations. Local pair projections need not be onto intrinsic groups.

claims.name: Finite solution groups and restrictions
claims.statement: Sol(S) is a finite subgroup, and restriction from a larger finite fibre set sends solutions to solutions. In general it is not surjective. Empty S has its unique empty tuple.

claims.name: Global binary patching gives the actual restriction isomorphism
claims.statement: rho is an injective group homomorphism. Any product tuple satisfying every local H_CD condition assembles into one bijection of ALL points, preserving every relation in both directions by arity<=2. It lies in N, so rho identifies N exactly with the global pair-CSP solution group, including empty X. No homogeneity or countability is used.

claims.name: Actual binding marginals are globally subdirect and reconstruct N
claims.statement: P_CD is subdirect over actual B_C,B_D by definition of those images, even when B_C is proper in H_C. The full family satisfying all ACTUAL P_CD conditions lies in the local CSP and hence in rho(N); conversely every actual N tuple satisfies them. This global reconstruction does not assert an analogous finite projection identity.

claims.name: Countable exhaustion and nonempty finite solution levels
claims.statement: For finite S and one fixed tuple g on S, assume EVERY finite T containing S admits a solution restricting to g. A countable exhaustion T_n yields nonempty finite levels of such solutions; restriction connects successive levels. No coherent family is assumed in the premise; finitely many fibres are handled directly.

claims.name: Explicit finite-continuation path construction
claims.statement: For the solution tree with finite levels of C06, level zero is the singleton prescribed tuple g and every later node restricts to it. Thus the root has arbitrarily long continuations. Among finitely many children of an infinitely continuing node one has arbitrarily long continuations, else finitely many failure levels would give a common bound. Recursively choose it to obtain a coherent path. Finite fibre families were handled directly; no external Konig theorem is imported.

claims.name: Compact projection exact quantifiers
claims.statement: A tuple g on finite S is in pr_S rho(N) iff for EVERY finite T>=S there EXISTS h in Sol(T) restricting to that SAME g. Sufficiency uses C07; union of its coherent path satisfies each global pair constraint and hence C04. Necessity is restriction. This also means a nonextendible tuple has one finite obstruction T.

claims.name: Relative owner homogeneity removes hidden finite constraints
claims.statement: Under A04 a tuple in Sol(S) is a finite partial isomorphism on the whole selected fibre union, preserving every owner predicate. Homogeneity extends it to Aut(X^own)=N, proving pr_S N=Sol(S), B_C=H_C and P_CD=H_CD. This does not follow from homogeneity of X alone.

claims.name: Finite pair annihilators define the global kernel
claims.statement: For intrinsic H_C=V_C, each H_CD is exactly the kernel of its finite-dimensional annihilator, even if nonsubdirect. Span all those rows in D to form R; global patching gives rho(N)=R^perp. Unary-supported defining rows are allowed only when true for the relevant local groups; for one isolated fibre R=0.

claims.name: Countable linear-functional separation without compactness
claims.statement: The direct sum D is countable from A03 and finite coordinate duals. If ell is outside R, define f(r+epsilon ell)=epsilon on R+<ell>. Enumerate D and extend f one vector at a time, assigning zero to each newly independent vector. Its union is linear on D, zero on R and one on ell. No Zorn or new separation provider is required.

claims.name: Algebraic dual of finite-support tests is the full product
claims.statement: A linear f:D->F2 restricts to each finite V_C*, hence evaluates at a unique x_C in V_C by the explicit finite-bidual basis formula. Conversely each product tuple evaluates all finite-support tests. Thus Hom(D,F2) is canonically the FULL product, with no finite-support restriction on x.

claims.name: Double annihilator and restricted projection formula
claims.statement: C11/C12 separate every ell outside R from R by an actual product tuple in R^perp, so Ann(R^perp)=R. A test supported on finite S annihilates pr_S N iff its zero-extension annihilates N; hence Ann(pr_S N)=R intersect D_S.

claims.name: Finite marginal constraints span their exact test rows
claims.statement: On finite S, imposing every actual singleton B_C and pair P_CD marginal has annihilator span{R intersect D_T: T subset S, |T|<=2}, by C13 and finite-dimensional duality. The pair groups here are actual projections, not arbitrary intrinsic H_CD; singleton constraints must remain for |S|=1.

claims.name: Width-two criterion iff actual finite projection has only marginal constraints
claims.statement: Both pr_S N and the group satisfying its singleton/pair marginals are finite-dimensional subspaces. They are equal iff their annihilators coincide, equivalently R intersect D_S is generated by its support<=2 subspaces inside S. Empty S gives zero test space and one empty motion. No arbitrary-variable elimination claim is made.

claims.name: Full restriction to an entire named finite sort is onto
claims.statement: Under A06 any automorphism of finite induced P_i is an actual finite partial isomorphism of X, so homogeneity extends it. Thus full Gamma->R_i is onto and each ACTUAL P_ij is subdirect over the intrinsic R_i,R_j. Empty named sorts, if allowed, give the trivial group.

claims.name: Strong finite projection on entire named sorts
claims.statement: For finite S, union of g_i in intrinsic R_i whose every pair is an actual P_ij motion is a bijection of the finite full named-sort union. Actual pair witnesses preserve every cross binary relation, intrinsic maps preserve internal/unary relations; homogeneity gives one full Gamma extension. This includes empty and singleton S, and does not require an F partition or countability.

claims.name: Linear Goursat representation of actual subdirect pairs
claims.statement: For an actual subdirect P_ij<=V_i times V_j, let N_i={(x,0) in P_ij}, N_j similarly. Pair membership defines a canonical linear isomorphism V_i/N_i -> V_j/N_j. Using one common W_ij gives surjective maps pi_ij,rho_ij with P_ij={(x,y):pi_ij(x)=rho_ij(y)}. The trivial quotient for a full product is allowed.

claims.name: Named finite image equals check-map kernel and rank count
claims.statement: Under A07 the actual full Gamma image on finite S is ker Phi_S by C17/C18. Rank-nullity gives its cardinality 2^(sum_i dim V_i - rank Phi_S). This counts the finite IMAGE, not the full possibly infinite Gamma. Empty and singleton S have no pair rows.

claims.name: Flat graph transport from actual full-group lifts
claims.statement: If the actual pair images on three distinct entire finite named sorts are graphs of isomorphisms theta_ij, theta_ik and theta_jk, extend any chosen g_i to Gamma by C16. Its simultaneous three restrictions force theta_ik=theta_jk composed with theta_ij. This argument does not need elementary-abelian groups and does not apply to freely chosen pair maps.

claims.name: Actual hidden-parity binary countercontrol
claims.statement: On A=B=C=F2 and D=F2², the canonical binary orbital structure of shifts (u,v,u+v,(u,v)) has actual automorphism group these four shifts. Its ABC pair marginals are unrestricted, but its ABC projection is the even-parity subgroup; a lone A flip on A union B union C is a partial binary isomorphism with no global extension. Thus the source is not homogeneous and hidden width-three elimination is real.

claims.name: Homogeneous moving-owner countercontrol with intrinsic/binding gap
claims.statement: For X=S3 name every R_g(x,y) iff y=xg. Its full group is left translations, and every nonempty partial isomorphism extends by the translation f(x0)x0^-1, so X is homogeneous. F has left cosets of a transposition subgroup H as three moving two-point classes. Owner-kernel core(H) is trivial, while each intrinsic H_C is C2. Naming the individual owners destroys homogeneity; local pair groups on distinct owners are trivial and not subdirect over H_C. No CCO or SAP claim is made.

review.remaining: Receiving projects must implement finite induced automorphisms, countable tree/functional extension and all exact restriction/dual maps. No source-specific exact-owner or finer-action lifting theorem is supplied.

overview_mermaid: B["Actual binary relational source"] --> N["Global owner-kernel patching"]
H["Owner-named homogeneity"] --> R["Local Sol equals finite projection"]
A["Entire finite named sorts"] --> E["Full-group finite image"]
overview_notes: Global binary patching never implies the finite projected pair formula without its extra criterion.
Relative owner homogeneity and full homogeneous entire named sorts are separate hypotheses, not consequences of naming owners.
The countable tree and countable separation are expanded internally; no CCO or phase-seed provider is imported.
